definition: Cast-off coverings: especially the shed skin, shell, feathers, or other outer layer of an animal; by extension, anything discarded after serving its season.
etymology: Latin exuviae first meant clothes stripped off or left behind, from exuere, “to strip off.” Naturalists borrowed the image for the husks creatures leave behind.
usage: The path was bright with the exuviae of summer: curled leaves, empty seedpods, and papery wings.
